subject: Dedicated capacity sizing and SLO fit for Caldera Systems — commitment review
messages:
From: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@caldera.ai>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated pool ask — SLO & throughput targets

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a new patient-facing summarization feature and need committed capacity numbers to take to procurement. High level asks:

- SLO: 95th latency <= 350ms for user-visible responses (we estimate average response length ~120 tokens).
- Peak concurrency: up to 80 concurrent active user requests at peak (web chat flows).
- Expected steady monthly tokens: ~180M tokens (we'll finalize after the pilot).
- Multi-region: primary in us-west, fallback in us-east.

Can you provide a conservative GPU slab recommendation (SKU, GPUs, expected tokens/sec per slab), suggested headroom percentage, and any operational mitigations (caching, quantization, model variant) that materially change the sizing? We’ll need this broken down for a 12-month committed plan.

Thanks,
Asha
Asha Reddy
Head of Platform
Caldera Systems

On behalf of Tom W.

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@caldera.ai>, Tom Whitaker <tom.whitaker@caldera.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool ask — SLO & throughput targets

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear brief. Opening a quick thread with our sizing sketch and assumptions. Ben and Priyom have run an initial model to translate your concurrency/SLO into tokens/sec and GPU counts; Marcus will chime in on the quantization and fallback variants.

Summary (quick answers up front):
- Recommended committed slab (H100-backed reserved pool): 10 GPUs (H100 80GB) to meet your 95th <= 350ms SLO at peak with ~20% ops headroom.
- Alternative cost-optimized: 8x A100-80GB with aggressive KV caching + q4_0 quantized 13B model (expected ~15% latency increase vs H100 but ~18% lower unit cost).
- Key mitigations: proactive KV prefix caching for dialogs (reduces non-prefix tokens by ~40%), model variant routing (13B quantized for typical chats, 33B FP16 only for long-form summaries), and burst fallback to hosted pool for extreme spikes.

See attached caldera_capacity_model_v3.xlsx for the math. I pasted the headline calculations below. If this matches what procurement wants, we can lock a committed quote and map to a monthly tokens estimate.

—Sofia

--- Headline sizing calculations (assumptions) ---
- avg response tokens: 120 tokens
- target p95 latency: 350ms = 0.35s
- peak concurrency: 80 active requests

Tokens/sec required at peak (no cache): concurrency * avg_tokens / p95_seconds = 80 * 120 / 0.35 = 27,428 t/s

Per-GPU sustained throughput (measured on our internal benchmark for quantized 13B chat workloads):
- H100 80GB (opt kernels, q4_0): ~4,500 tokens/sec (sustained, 512 context, chat-steady)
- A100 80GB (opt kernels, q4_0): ~3,300 tokens/sec

Raw GPU count (no headroom):
- H100: ceil(27,428 / 4,500) = 7 GPUs
- A100: ceil(27,428 / 3,300) = 9 GPUs

Operational headroom and safety policy (recommended): +20% steady headroom + 2-GPU spare for maintenance/failover ->
- H100 reserved slab recommendation = 7 * 1.2 = 8.4 -> round up + spare => 10 GPUs
- A100 reserved slab recommendation = 9 * 1.2 = 10.8 -> round up + spare => 12 GPUs (or 8 GPUs if you accept burst to hosted)

Cache impact: with KV/prefix caching applied to chat flows (estimated 40% reduction in tokens emitted to the model), required t/s decreases to ~16,457 t/s => H100 count drops to 4. (We do not recommend sizing without cache unless you cannot guarantee cacheability.)

Notes: these numbers account for typical batching and concurrent request scheduling in our Dedicated runtime; p95 latency includes end-to-end model generation but excludes network egress to the browser (we add a 25ms network buffer typically).

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, Marcus_Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@caldera.ai>
Date: 2026-08-23T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool ask — Dedicated slab cost/ops tradeoffs

Asha / team — adding details on burst policy and ops considerations that change sizing/cost: 

- Burst policy: We can configure automatic burst to hosted pool for short-lived spikes (1–5 minutes). With burst enabled you can reduce committed GPUs by ~15–25% depending on acceptable burst volume. Pricing is usage-based for bursts.
- Autoscale timeline: Dedicated autoscale has a minimum scale step of 2 GPUs and a warm-up of ~90–120s for cold start on a new node image; for predictable daily peaks we prefer pre-warmed spare GPUs.
- Maintenance windows: we recommend a 2-GPU spare to ensure no SLO impact during rolling upgrades.

Costing quick note (very rough):
- H100 reserved slab (10 GPUs) — ballpark committed monthly compute fee: $Xk/month (I put line items in the spreadsheet).
- A100 reserved (12 GPUs) — ~12–18% cheaper on committed monthly compute, but heavier ops to meet 95th without cache.

If you want a lower committed price we can size at 8 H100 + burst to hosted for predictable spikes; that saves ~18% in commitment but shifts risk to burst spend.

—Ben

(Attachment: caldera_capacity_model_v3.xlsx — updated with burst scenarios and cost columns)

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@caldera.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-24T10:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool ask — latency tail breakdown and validation plan

Asha — quick note on validation and an example p95 breakdown we saw on a comparable healthcare deployment:

- Tail contributors (by % of p95 budget): model generation 72%, batching queue 12%, cold-starts 8%, network/ingest 8%.
- For your workload (short chat responses), reducing model-side tokens via prefix caching has the largest impact. We recommend a 2-week pilot with the following validation tests:
  1) Synthetic replay of your peak traffic (80 concurrency) using your average token distribution (attached spreadsheet includes a replay script snippet).
  2) End-to-end p95 measurement from us-west to your browser endpoints (we'll provide an agent).
  3) Cache hit-rate tuning: goal >=40% chat prefix hits during steady state.

If the pilot validates a >=40% cache hit rate we can lock pricing to the 8x H100 committed slab with a 5% buffer instead of 20% (saves you ~12% monthly).

—Priyom

- One-page summary: attached (caldera_slo_examples.pdf) — distilled numbers and 2 recommended commitment options (10x H100 conservative, 8x H100 pilot + burst to hosted).
- Pilot kickoff: We propose Monday 2026-08-31 for a 2-week pilot. Action items:
  - Caldera provides representative prompt set + expected concurrency windows (Asha).
  - Redwood to deploy pilot slab (8x H100) with KV caching instrumented and replay harness (Sofia/Ben).
  - Joint validation week 2: live p95 collection and cache hit-rate tuning (Priyom).

If that schedule works I'll loop in Contracts to draft the SOW and a provisional commitment term for review.

Thanks — excited to get this running.
